title: Urgent: Tail-latency spike after inference-optimizer rollout causing TTFT and TPS drops across deployments
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and an overall drop in tokens/sec after yesterday's inference-optimizer rollout (runtime-2.3.1). Symptoms appeared on Hosted and Dedicated clusters and as a config-sensitive issue in Private on-prem customers that use mixed-precision quantized models. Scope: affected ~4% of production traffic during peak; high-impact enterprise customers experienced >2x TTFT on cold-starts and 30-50% lower sustained tokens/sec. Models impacted include open models using kv-cache and mixed-precision kernels (gptj-family variants and trimmed Llama derivatives). Suspected cause: the new optimizer changes kernel selection ordering combined with a delayed async kernel prewarm path that regresses cold-path loading and increases variance for the first few tokens on a request. This interacts badly with cross-model batching heuristics introduced in the same release, causing sporadic oversize batches and head-of-line blocking.
timeline: 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Pager alert: increased 95th/99th TTFT on hosted-prod-03 cluster
2026-03-10 03:28 UTC - First customer escalation from AcmeHealth (Dedicated) reporting 2.3x TTFT on chat endpoint
2026-03-10 03:45 UTC - Incident channel #infra-ppf opened; initial hypothesis: optimizer rollout (runtime-2.3.1) coincident with change to kernel selection order
2026-03-10 04:10 UTC - Reproduced in staging with synthetic load: significant TTFT spike on cold prefix when kernel prewarm deferred
2026-03-10 05:05 UTC - Short-term mitigation: disabled new kernel-selection gating on hosted canary, partially rolled back in Dedicated for affected customers
2026-03-10 06:40 UTC - Monitoring patch deployed to add granular metrics: kernel-load-latency, batch-size-distribution, head-of-line-wait
2026-03-11 11:00 UTC - Private customer (GovCorp) confirmed similar regression after applying 2.3.1 package on-prem; provided kernel debug logs
2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Narrowed root cause: race in async prewarm path plus fallback kernel path that serializes on first tile compilation
2026-03-12 13:15 UTC - Hotfix PR opened to enforce eager prewarm for hot model families and avoid cross-model batch aggregation for first-token windows
2026-03-13 02:00 UTC - Hotfix candidate deployed to hosted canary and one Dedicated pool; metrics show TTFT back within SLO for canary traffic
mitigation: Rolled back kernel-selection reordering on 3 hosted canaries and 2 Dedicated reservations (quick revert) - reduces cold TTFT but does not address batching interaction
Added config flag runtime.experimental.avoid_cross_model_first_window=true and enabled for affected tenants to prevent oversized cross-model batches during first-token windows
For Private customers, provided temporary packaging with kernel prewarm enabled (package runtime-2.3.1-prewarm) and instructions to set prewarm_threads=4
Increased alerting sensitivity on kernel-load-latency and established a temporary autoscaling-policy that favors warm instances for high-SLA tenants
root_cause_summary: A regression in the optimizer's kernel selection ordering introduced a fallback path that triggers an async kernel prewarm. Under cross-model batching heuristics, this allowed oversized batches that serialized on a single thread for tile compilation on cold paths. The combined effect produced high tail latency for TTFT and reduced overall token throughput while the system waited for kernel compilation and prewarm to complete.
action_items: (A1) Merge and roll runtime hotfix that forces eager kernel prewarm for flagged model families (owner: Emma Chen) - target 2026-03-13 deploy
(A2) Rework cross-model batching fallback to respect first-token windows and avoid grouping heterogeneous model precisions (owner: Ravi Patel) - RFC due 2026-03-17
(A3) Add unit and integration tests that simulate mixed-precision cold-starts and assert TTFT thresholds (owner: QA Team) - estimate 5
(A4) Postmortem doc and customer communication draft for AcmeHealth, GovCorp and two other impacted customers (owner: Miguel Alvarez) - due 2026-03-14
(A5) Long-term: consider kernel compilation cache warmers and persistent prewarm pool for high-SLA tenants (owner: Research/Infra) - proposal 2026-04-01
